neighbours.label: the 'for' that gives the reason a text was altered ('edited for clarity', 'shortened for brevity')
fire: This conversation has been trimmed for readability.
Some answers were lightly edited for flow.
Her remarks have been abridged for publication.
The following excerpt was shortened for clarity and length.
Letters may be edited for content and tone.
The exchange has been condensed for clarity by our staff.
His comments were edited for accuracy after the call.
Both speeches have been reworded for consistency.
quiet: This conversation has been recorded for a friend.
Some answers were lightly written in pencil by students.
Her remarks have been printed by the local paper.
The following excerpt was chosen by the editor.
Letters may be mailed for free at the front desk.
The exchange has been scheduled for Friday by our staff.
His comments were made for the cameras after the call.
Both speeches have been translated by volunteers.

notes: ' for' is the most common peak token. Passive editing verbs fire it strongly; 'for' after other verbs (paid for, left for, a gift for) stays near zero, and even active 'edited a book for her publisher' stays quiet. Weaker fire on 'for the sake of' suggests a wider 'for a purpose' reading that this test does not cover.
